citation: Borman, G. D., Slavin, R. E., Cheung, A. C. K., Chamberlain, A. M., Madden, N. A., & Chambers, B. (2007). Final reading outcomes of the national randomized field trial of Success for All. American Educational Research Journal, 44(3), 701-731. https://doi.org/10.3102/0002831207306743
design: Cluster-randomized trial (RCT); assignment unit = School; 35 schools analyzed at Year 3 (18 Success for All experimental, 17 control) drawn from an originally randomized 41-school sample across 11 states; subject = Reading/early literacy; grade band K-2 (baseline kindergarten cohort tracked through spring of grade 2). TPD = Success for All comprehensive whole-school reading reform, delivered with 3 days initial training + ~16 days first-year on-site coaching/follow-up and ~15 days/year thereafter from Success for All Foundation trainers (program facilitator, ongoing PD, quarterly fidelity visits). Control = business-as-usual; control schools could purchase/implement any innovation other than Success for All. Within-school design: each school implemented SFA in either grades K-2 or grades 3-5 (randomly assigned); K-2 grades in the 3-5-assigned schools served as controls. Year-3 analysis is restricted to the baseline kindergarten cohort because by Year 3 no valid no-treatment control remained for the baseline first-grade cohort.
problems: Source is the program-developer/author-hosted full accepted manuscript of the published AERJ article on the Success for All Foundation site (co-authors Slavin, Chamberlain, Madden, Chambers are SFAF-affiliated); it carries the full published citation on its title page and contains the complete methods, results, and all tables (Tables 1-5). The journal version (SAGE) is paywalled and OpenAlex/Unpaywall report no OA; the White Rose institutional record has no deposited full text and ERIC (EJ782058) hosts no full text, so this developer-hosted copy is the only legal open copy located. Effect sizes in Tables 3 and 4 are STANDARDIZED HLM impact coefficients (the literacy outcomes were standardized to ~unit variance; intercepts ~0, within-school variance ~0.84), i.e. the SFA-assignment 'Effect' column is itself the standardized mean difference d, with its SE on the same standardized scale; these equal the Year-3 effect sizes in Table 5. d is already pretest-adjusted (school-mean PPVT covariate) and cluster-adjusted (school-level HLM), so cluster_adjusted=true and the impact SE is used directly for g_se. No intraclass correlation (ICC) / design effect is reported anywhere in the paper, so icc is left null (NOT guessed). The report gives no single composite/total reading score: the three Woodcock Reading Mastery Tests subtests (Word Identification, Word Attack, Passage Comprehension) are treated as three co-equal primary literacy outcomes (all marked primary, none a composite of the others). Two analytic samples are reported: (1) the combined longitudinal + in-mover 'school-wide' sample = the full analytic sample (1,085 treatment + 1,023 control = 2,108 students; Table 4 / Table 5 School-wide Year 3), extracted as the full-sample primary contrasts; (2) the three-year longitudinal sample (n=1,445; Table 3 / Table 5 Longitudinal Year 3), a non-random persister subset (students present all three years), extracted as subgroup with is_full_sample=false. The longitudinal sample's per-condition n split is not reported, so n_t/n_c are null for those rows (the full school-wide split is 1,085/1,023). The small-sample correction J is ~1.000 at these N's, so g essentially equals the reported d; J was computed from total analytic N (student-level SMD convention) and is negligible. Timepoint = Year 3 spring (end of grade 2), the immediate/final post wave; Year 1 (grade K) and Year 2 (grade 1) waves are noted but not extracted.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Success for All (TPD-supported whole-school comprehensive reading reform) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Woodcock Reading Mastery Tests - Revised (WMRT) Word Attack subtest (phonemic decoding of nonsense words; nationally normed)
effect_sizes.timepoint: Year 3 post (spring 2005, end of grade 2); immediate/final post wave
effect_sizes.g_method: Impact is the standardized HLM fixed-effect coefficient for SFA assignment from Table 4 (combined longitudinal + in-mover 'school-wide' sample); outcomes were standardized so the coefficient is itself d = 0.36 with SE = 0.11 (matches Table 5 School-wide Year 3 = 0.36). Hedges' g = J*d, J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = n_t+n_c-2 = 2106, J = 0.99964, g = 0.3599. g_se = J*impact_se = 0.99964*0.11 = 0.1100; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.01209. Standardized via the pooled within-sample SD of the outcome (the model's standardization), pretest-adjusted by school-mean PPVT covariate, cluster-adjusted via school-level HLM.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 4 (p. 50 of PDF / journal p. 50); Table 5 School-wide Year 3 (p. 51); results text p. 28-29; sample sizes p. 23-24
effect_sizes.notes: Full analytic ('school-wide') sample: 1,085 treatment + 1,023 control = 2,108 students in 35 schools (18 SFA, 17 control). Significant at p<.01 (t=3.27). Largest of the three literacy effects; Word Attack measures phonemic awareness/decoding, the domain SFA's kindergarten phonics instruction targets first. d=0.36 corresponds to Cohen's U3 of ~64th percentile (text p. 33). WMRT is nationally normed, independent of the developer. One of three co-equal primary literacy outcomes (no composite reported).
